# Reri — Ptolemaic funerary papyrus, EA75044,4

## Identity, edition and scope

The primary object is British Museum EA75044,4, fragments of Reri’s Book of the Dead in hieratic, from Thebes and catalogued as Ptolemaic. The Western Australian Museum’s joint exhibition article by Moya Smith, with spell titles/translations attributed to British Museum curator John Taylor, bounds the period as 305–30 BCE. This is a period attribution, not a precise production year. Read the complete WA Museum discussion and the search-indexed British Museum catalogue description; direct British Museum catalogue access returned 403. The latter retrieval is saved separately as `working/sources-texts-references/primary-texts/E4-arabic-egyptian-2026-09-08/reri-bm-search-indexed-record.json`. The admitted practice is the physically identified arrangement of spells; the full hieratic wording has not been independently transcribed or translated.

<a id="reri-ptolemaic-funerary-papyrus-p001"></a>
### reri-ptolemaic-funerary-papyrus-p001 — Remembering the deceased’s name

**Paraphrase:** On EA75044,4, spell 25 occupies the top of column 3 and concerns the deceased remembering his name. It lies in a sequence that restores speech and protects the heart.

**Locator:** EA75044,4, column 3 top, spell 25; WA Museum discussion of spells 21–31 and 33.

**Provenance:** WA Museum complete Reri article, with the search-indexed British Museum catalogue identifying the object. Read 2026-09-08 against the identified online witness.

**Source relation:** Paraphrased.

**Status:** paraphrase-ready; no quotation admitted.

**Use boundary:** The article explains this remembrance as preserving continued life within the funerary conception. That is an attributed ritual purpose, not evidence of survival after death. Its illustrative wording for other spells is drawn from a revised Faulkner translation of Ani; it must not be cited as a transcription of Reri. No Ani/Reri conflation or universal Egyptian soul-component scheme.
